plan: Hard-item experiment: dissolved-vs-resolved vocabulary, base-rate reasoning, subordinate-clause boundary punctuation, an only-when interaction data item, and a vocabulary item whose trap fits half the context.

passages.title: Mathematical objects
passages.text: Philosopher Ana Ruiz contends that the long debate over whether mathematical objects truly exist has not been settled so much as ______: once the debate's key terms are clarified, she argues, the two sides turn out to be making compatible claims in different vocabularies.

passages.title: Cat domestication
passages.text: Early accounts portrayed the domestication of cats as deliberate: people, it was said, tamed wild cats to protect stored grain from rodents. Genetic studies have complicated this picture. Domestic cats show far fewer genetic differences from their wild ancestors than domestic dogs do from theirs, and those differences arose gradually over thousands of years. Some researchers now argue that cats largely domesticated themselves, tolerating people in exchange for easy access to prey, long before humans took any deliberate role in their breeding.

passages.title: Base rates
passages.text: In a survey of people who had developed a certain digestive condition, 80% reported regularly drinking a popular brand of sparkling water. A commentator cited this figure as evidence that the drink may cause the condition. But in the population as a whole, about 80% of people also report regularly drinking that brand, which suggests that ______

passages.title: Halted trial
passages.text: The trial of the new medication was halted ______ the results had looked promising, a safety concern emerged in the final month that the researchers could not explain.

passages.title: Commute times
passages.text: City officials had hoped the new express lanes would sharply reduce commute times, but the effect proved modest. ______ the average weekday trip into downtown shortened by only about two minutes.

passages.title: Opera notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Composer Inés Morales wrote the opera Salt Road (1998).
• Composer Daniel Oyelaran wrote the opera Harbor Lights (2004).
• Salt Road is set in a nineteenth-century mining town; Harbor Lights is set in a modern port city.
• Both composers built their operas from folk melodies they had collected from local singers.
• Salt Road is scored for full orchestra; Harbor Lights is scored for nine players.

passages.title: Fertilizer and water
passages.text:
Researchers grew corn in plots that received different amounts of fertilizer and water.
Fertilizer | Yield with low water (bushels) | Yield with high water (bushels)
None | 20 | 30
Low | 21 | 38
High | 20 | 46
The researchers concluded that fertilizer increased yield only when water was plentiful.

passages.title: Archive catalog
passages.text: Researchers hoping to use the archive's catalog to find letters on particular subjects have been frustrated: the catalog is ______, listing every letter's date and sender but saying nothing about what any letter contains.

passages.title: Bird counts
passages.text: Since the wetlands at the Maple Creek reserve were restored a decade ago, the number of bird species recorded there each spring ______ risen every year, according to volunteers who conduct the annual count.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: the two sides turn out to be making compatible claims in different vocabularies
candidates.explanation: The debate is not settled (no side wins) but disappears once the terms are clear, because the sides never truly disagreed. To make a problem vanish rather than solve it is to "dissolve" it.

A.rationale: "Resolved" means settled in favor of an answer, but the text says the debate has "not been settled."

B.rationale: Clarifying terms reveals agreement, which calms rather than intensifies the debate.

D.rationale: Nothing suggests the debate is delayed; Ruiz says its apparent disagreement disappears.

hints: What happens to a disagreement that turns out to be only about words?

strategy.explanation: Predict "made to disappear rather than answered," then match.

candidates.remember: Settling a debate differs from showing it was never real.

candidates.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the argument made by "some researchers" in the text?

choices.A: Remains from the earliest farming villages show that people confined and selectively bred cats from the start.
choices.B: Domestic cats today hunt rodents in much the same way that their wild ancestors did.
choices.C: Wild cats in some regions still scavenge for food near human settlements today.
choices.D: The genetic differences between domestic and wild cats accumulated over many millennia.

candidates.evidence: long before humans took any deliberate role in their breeding
candidates.explanation: The argument is that cats came to people on their own and humans bred them deliberately only much later. Evidence of deliberate confinement and breeding from the very start contradicts that sequence.

B.rationale: Unchanged hunting behavior fits the idea that cats changed little and on their own.

C.rationale: Wild cats approaching people on their own fits self-domestication.

D.rationale: This repeats the text's evidence for gradual, self-driven change.

hints: What does the argument say about when humans began breeding cats?

strategy.explanation: For each finding, ask whether it fits or conflicts with self-domestication.

candidates.remember: To weaken a claim, contradict its key condition.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the drink most likely protects people against developing the condition.
choices.B: most people who drink the brand will eventually develop the condition.
choices.C: the condition is far more common than researchers had previously thought.
choices.D: the survey result offers little evidence that the drink raises the risk of the condition.

candidates.evidence: about 80% of people also report regularly drinking that brand
candidates.explanation: If 80% of everyone drinks the brand, finding that 80% of people with the condition drink it is exactly what chance alone predicts, so the figure gives no evidence of a link.

A.rationale: Equal rates show no association in either direction, not a protective effect.

B.rationale: The figures say nothing about how many drinkers develop the condition.

C.rationale: Nothing in the text concerns how common the condition is.

hints: Compare the 80% among patients with the 80% among everyone.
What would you expect if the drink had no effect at all?

strategy.explanation: Predict: the figure is what you'd expect by chance.

candidates.remember: A rate means little without the base rate to compare.

candidates.subskill: Sentence boundaries with a subordinate clause
candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: a safety concern emerged in the final month
candidates.explanation: "Although the results had looked promising" is a subordinate clause attached to the main clause "a safety concern emerged." That full sentence must be separated from "The trial ... was halted early," which is also complete: a period does it.

B.rationale: This joins "The trial ... was halted early" to a second independent clause ("a safety concern emerged") with only a comma, a comma splice.

C.rationale: A comma should not follow "although," which introduces a clause.

D.rationale: The two independent clauses run together without punctuation.

hints: How many independent clauses are there?

strategy.explanation: Find each subject-verb pair that can stand alone, then check the boundary.

candidates.remember: An "although" clause attaches to the clause after it, not before.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.explanation: The second sentence gives the precise figure behind "modest": two minutes. "Specifically" introduces such a detail.

A.rationale: "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the second sentence spells out the modest effect.

B.rationale: "Even so" signals something true despite the prior point, but the sentence restates it with detail.

C.rationale: A two-minute change is a measure of the modest effect, not a result of it.

hints: Does the second sentence contrast with, result from, or detail the first?
candidates.remember: Detail that pins down a general claim calls for "specifically."

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the two composers' methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Morales set Salt Road in a nineteenth-century mining town, but Oyelaran set Harbor Lights in a modern port.
choices.B: Morales and Oyelaran both built their operas from folk melodies they had collected from local singers.
choices.C: Salt Road (1998) and Harbor Lights (2004) are operas by Inés Morales and Daniel Oyelaran, respectively.
choices.D: Unlike Morales, who wrote Salt Road for full orchestra, Oyelaran scored Harbor Lights for just nine players.

candidates.evidence: Both composers built their operas from folk melodies they had collected from local singers.
candidates.explanation: The goal is a similarity in method; only the folk-melody note describes how both composers worked in the same way.

A.rationale: This is a difference in setting, not a similarity in method.

C.rationale: This identifies the works but describes no method.

D.rationale: This is a difference in scoring.

hints: Which notes describe how the composers worked?

strategy.explanation: Check each choice for both "similarity" and "method."

candidates.remember: A goal can require both a relationship and a topic.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.A: The highest yield in the study, 46 bushels, came from plots given high fertilizer and high water.
choices.B: With low water, yield varied only between 20 and 21 bushels across the three fertilizer levels.
choices.C: With high water, yield rose from 30 to 46 as fertilizer increased, but with low water it stayed near 20.
choices.D: For every level of fertilizer, plots with high water outyielded plots with low water.

candidates.evidence: fertilizer increased yield only when water was plentiful
candidates.explanation: "Only when" needs both halves: fertilizer helps with high water (30 to 46) and does not with low water (about 20). C gives both.

A.rationale: This shows the best combination but not that fertilizer had no effect under low water.

B.rationale: This shows no effect under low water but not the effect under high water.

D.rationale: This concerns water's effect, not whether fertilizer's effect depends on water.

hints: The conclusion has two parts: helps with high water, not with low.

strategy.explanation: Translate "only when" into two conditions to check.

candidates.remember: "Only when" claims need evidence for both conditions.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: listing every letter's date and sender but saying nothing about what any letter contains
candidates.explanation: The catalog gives only the bare framework (date and sender) without content, and researchers are frustrated by it: it is "skeletal."

B.rationale: The catalog does list every letter, but the point is that its entries are bare; "exhaustive" praises its thoroughness.

C.rationale: Nothing suggests the dates or senders are wrong.

D.rationale: Nothing suggests the catalog cannot be read.

hints: Which word describes something that has only a bare outline?
candidates.remember: Use the frustration cue: the word must name a shortcoming.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: the number of bird species recorded there each spring
candidates.explanation: The subject is "the number," which is singular, so "has risen." ("A number of" would be plural; "the number of" is singular.)

A.rationale: "The number" is singular; "species" is the object of "of."

B.rationale: "Having" leaves the sentence without a main verb.

C.rationale: "Are" is plural and does not form "risen" correctly.

hints: What is the head noun of the subject?

strategy.explanation: Find the head noun, then match the verb.

candidates.remember: "The number of" is singular; "a number of" is plural.
